properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. It is dev_storyflow's wish #50 (session f56683f3, 2026-09-27 evening, their first full session on flo2.io, reflow2 0.72.0), triaged 2026-09-28 from art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27. In their words: "A recency view: the design's changes (ChangeEvents, Decisions, Verifications, facts) newest first. It needs a stored created/updated date on nodes; where-am-i's 'since last time' needs the same."

WHY IT CAME UP: the issue beside it is root-caused in fact:root-cause-no-served-read-answers-since-last-time-2026-09-28. No served read orders anything by time. The accepted req:what-changed-since-i-looked-and-by-whom is marked satisfied by changelog_view, which answers a narrower question. A same-day re-walk replayed on scratch was invisible to changelog_view and to loop_status since_export. The reporter's first where-am-i summary missed exactly that.

WHAT IS ALREADY STORED, measured on reflow2's own design: ChangeEvent.detected_at on 563 of 1158; TemporalFact.valid_from on 614 of 708; Verification.last_run_at on 294 of 349. No Decision carries a date on the node (0 of 829); 534 are dated only through authored_at or approved_at on their AUTHORED_BY edge. There is no write time anywhere, and the hosted engine's automatic crediting draws its author edge with no date.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE REPORTER'S: store a created/updated date on every node, stamped by the server at write time, and serve a newest-first view over it. Cheap to compute once stored, and it answers "since last time" for revisions as well as creations. What it costs is the principle below.
(b) A READ-ONLY VIEW OVER THE DATES ALREADY STORED. Merge detected_at, valid_from, last_run_at and the AUTHORED_BY dates newest first, and give each type an explicit count of what is undated instead of dropping it. Nothing new is written and nothing is invented. Weakness: half the ChangeEvents and most Decisions stay invisible, it orders by day rather than time, and a re-walk shows only if the caller moved last_run_at.
(c) AN ORDINAL ANSWER INSTEAD OF A CLOCK. A per-node monotonic revision (req:a-node-carries-a-revision, accepted, unbuilt) lets "since last time" become "since the revision or generation I last saw". The server already keeps a write generation for its memo. Weakness: no calendar ("the latest work was 09-26" still cannot be said), and it only works across restarts, imports and hosts if it is persisted.
(d) THE AUTOMATIC WRITE JOURNAL. A thin what-and-who floor under authored ChangeEvents (dec:idea-should-the-server-journal-every-write-itself; req:a-write-carries-who-made-it-and-the-server-records-that-it-happened, both proposed). A journal answers "what changed since T" by construction, and the recency view becomes a read over it.
(e) FIX THE PROMISE, NOT THE DATA. Bound where-am-i's "if nothing has changed since last time, say so" (and root-cause's "recent ChangeEvents") to what is computable: topic_report's `latest`, invalidated_findings, and since_export where a committed record exists. The skill then says plainly what it cannot see. This can be done whatever else is chosen.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, STATED FAIRLY: the core takes no clock, on purpose. The core reads a clock only at the edge, for arithmetic such as age_days, and "inventing a date would be a claim nobody made" (req:defaults-do-not-assert; record_change's own comment). dec:loop-status-state-not-history refuses run history because "looking is not writing". claim_region and coverage_report make the CALLER supply the date. A server-stamped time would be the first date the design asserts on its own authority. Its weaknesses are concrete:
· An import or merge would stamp the day of the import over the design's real history (a 5,668-node design all dated today).
· The time would read as when the thing HAPPENED, when it only records when it was WRITTEN.
· Every write would change the export, the content hash and the per-node files that git merges.
The case FOR is also real. A write time is a fact the server itself witnessed, unlike detected_at. And the design's own measurement is that a clockless "since" is not computable at all: fact:record-change-places-an-event-by-epoch-and-212-of-214-epochs-carry-no-date, and "only 2 of 2,367 nodes carry created_at". Options (b), (c) and (e) keep the principle intact; (a) and (d) revise it. That choice is the owner's.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 serve a recency view listing the design's changes (ChangeEvents, Decisions, Verifications, facts) newest first, so where-am-i's "since last time" has something to read? And does that need a stored created/updated date on every node, which the core has so far declined to invent?
properties.rationale: Recorded open because it turns on a standing principle (no clock in the core), and the options divide by whether they keep or revise it. The need itself is not new: it has been accepted intent since 2026-08-07 (req:what-changed-since-i-looked-and-by-whom), and the finding beside this idea shows the design currently reads that need as delivered. Settling it is Anthony's call.
